page.layout: One column of verse, set in the upper part of the page. Below it, a printer's ornament (no text). No page number, running head, catchword or signature.

main_text.p: Marte vel inuito, quâ valet arte, canit.
Albion est testis, cui prælia, cuíque triumphos
Marte vel inuito, quâ valet arte, dedit.
Tu quoque testis eris, lachrymas cui mittit, eodem
Marte vel inuito, quâ valet arte, suas.
Ergo quid hac faciet Iacomotius arte, benigno
Mauorte, inuito si facere ista poteft?
Atque suâ poterit ritè sonare lyrâ.
An dubitas Princeps? cessa dubitare, Melissus
Namque tibi affirmat, Bezáq; magnus, idem.
Adde quod his lectis, Dux Illustrissime, chartis,
Pro genio id poteris ipse videre tuo.
O rarum Heroem! multū est, quod perlegis ipsos
Vates, plus, quod eos ipse probare potes.

page.notes: The ornament below the verse is a printer's decoration and is not transcribed. The first line of the last couplet is printed "O rarum Heroem!" as shown; "Bezáq;" is copied as printed and is uncertain. The long s is rendered as plain s throughout, so "poteft" and "cessa" read as printed.
